FixedSignature.text:
/-
  The sorts and constructors of the fixed part of every F0 definition, as Lean data (STATEMENTS.md
  §1, "The prelude constant"). Reviewed layer; read by the step relation's vocabulary
  (Core.lean), the generator (Emit.lean) and the sort checker.

  Every krust kompile output carries the same prelude modules and, inside the user module, the
  same declarations of the builtin sorts, of the K sequence and of the generated configuration
  cells. The KORE text of that part is `prelude/f0-prelude.kore` (Prelude.lean reads it); the data
  below names its sorts and constructors, and `SpecChecks.lean` checks it against the text.
  This module imports nothing but Lean's `Init`.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace KCore

/-! ## Sorts of the fixed text (names without the `Sort` prefix) -/

/-- Hooked or token sorts, with their number of sort parameters. Their elements are domain values,
not constructor terms. -/
def baseSorts : List (String × Nat) :=
  [("Bool", 0), ("Int", 0), ("KConfigVar", 0), ("List", 0), ("MInt", 1), ("Map", 0), ("Set", 0)]

/-- The sorts of the generated configuration `<generatedTop> <k> $PGM </k> <generatedCounter> …`. -/
def cellSorts : List String :=
  ["GeneratedCounterCell", "GeneratedCounterCellOpt", "GeneratedTopCell",
   "GeneratedTopCellFragment", "KCell", "KCellOpt"]

/-- The configuration sort. -/
def topCellSort : String := "GeneratedTopCell"

/-! ## Constructors of the fixed text -/

/-- A constructor: KORE symbol, argument sorts, result sort. -/
structure CtorSig where
  name : String
  args : List String
  result : String
  deriving Repr, DecidableEq

def kCellLabel : String := "Lbl'-LT-'k'-GT-'"

/-- The constructors the fixed text declares (`constructor{}()`), in declaration order. The k cell
`<k>` is declared by `emit` (its location is the configuration's), the others are in the text. -/
def fixedCtors : List CtorSig :=
  [⟨"kseq", ["KItem", "K"], "K"⟩, ⟨"dotk", [], "K"⟩,
   ⟨"Lbl'Hash'KConfigValue", ["K"], "KItem"⟩,
   ⟨kCellLabel, ["K"], "KCell"⟩,
   ⟨"Lbl'-LT-'generatedCounter'-GT-'", ["Int"], "GeneratedCounterCell"⟩,
   ⟨"Lbl'-LT-'generatedTop'-GT-'", ["KCell", "GeneratedCounterCell"], "GeneratedTopCell"⟩,
   ⟨"LblnoKCell", [], "KCellOpt"⟩,
   ⟨"LblnoGeneratedCounterCell", [], "GeneratedCounterCellOpt"⟩,
   ⟨"Lbl'-LT-'generatedTop'-GT-'-fragment", ["KCellOpt", "GeneratedCounterCellOpt"],
     "GeneratedTopCellFragment"⟩]

/-- Subsorts of the fixed text other than `X < KItem` (which holds for every sort below KItem). -/
def fixedSubsorts : List (String × String) :=
  [("KCell", "KCellOpt"), ("GeneratedCounterCell", "GeneratedCounterCellOpt")]

/-- The base sorts below KItem (all but the parametric MInt). -/
def baseSortsBelowKItem : List String := ["Bool", "Int", "KConfigVar", "List", "Map", "Set"]

end KCore

Core.text:
/-
  The semantic core of a K definition (STATEMENTS.md §1, the `Semantics` part of `Definition`):
  what the step relation reads. Reviewed layer; imports nothing but Lean's `Init` (and the fixed
  signature, FixedSignature.lean).

  A `Semantics` describes the user part of a kompiled definition at the level of the KORE
  kompile emits, over the fixed configuration
  `<generatedTop> <k> $PGM:S </k> <generatedCounter> </generatedTop>`: sorts, constructors,
  subsorts, functions given as ordered clauses with an optional catch-all, rewrite rules, the
  sort of `$PGM`. Variables are indices, with their sorts.
  Below it: the signature that the core induces and that matching and the sort of a ground term
  read (all constructors, the subsort pairs, the subsort order).

  The rest of `Definition` (presentation and certificate, read by `emit` and `wf` only) is in
  Definition.lean; the conditions of `wf` are in DefinitionWf.lean.
  Every function here is total and structurally recursive; there is no fuel.
-/
import KcoreSpec.FixedSignature

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace KCore

/-! ## The core -/

/-- A term of a clause or a rule. Variables are indices into the clause's (rule's) variable list.
`app` applies a constructor or a function of the definition by its KORE symbol; `inj` is
`inj{SortA, SortB}`; `as t i` is the as-pattern `\and{s}(t, xᵢ)` (left-hand sides only). -/
inductive Term where
  | var (i : Nat)
  | app (f : String) (args : List Term)
  | inj (a b : String) (t : Term)
  | as (t : Term) (i : Nat)
  deriving Repr, Inhabited

/-- A clause `f(p₁, …, pₙ) = rhs`; `vars` are the sorts of its variables (sort names without the
`Sort` prefix). -/
structure Clause where
  vars : List String
  pats : List Term
  rhs : Term
  deriving Repr

/-- The catch-all clause `f(x₁, …, xₙ) = rhs [owise]`: its i-th argument pattern is the variable
i, so it applies wherever no other clause does. -/
structure Owise where
  vars : List String
  rhs : Term
  deriving Repr

/-- A function: its signature, its clauses in order, and an optional catch-all clause. -/
structure Fn where
  label : String
  args : List String
  result : String
  clauses : List Clause
  owise : Option Owise
  deriving Repr

/-- A rewrite rule `lhs => rhs` between configurations (requires and ensures are `\top`). -/
structure Rule where
  vars : List String
  lhs : Term
  rhs : Term
  deriving Repr

structure Semantics where
  userSorts : List String
  /-- in declaration order -/
  ctors : List CtorSig
  /-- in declaration order: a function may call the ones before it -/
  fns : List Fn
  /-- the declared subsorts `(A, B)`, `A < B` -/
  userSubsorts : List (String × String)
  /-- the sort of `$PGM` in `<k> $PGM:S </k>` -/
  pgmSort : String
  rules : List Rule
  deriving Repr

/-! ## The signature the core induces -/

/-- Insertion of `a` into a list sorted by `key` (string order). -/
def insertBy {α : Type} (key : α → String) (a : α) : List α → List α
  | [] => [a]
  | b :: bs => if key a < key b then a :: b :: bs else b :: insertBy key a bs

def sortBy {α : Type} (key : α → String) (l : List α) : List α := l.foldr (insertBy key) []

namespace Semantics
variable (c : Semantics)

/-- Every sort below KItem, in string order. -/
def sortsBelowKItem : List String := sortBy id (baseSortsBelowKItem ++ cellSorts ++ c.userSorts)

/-- The subsort pairs `(A, B)`, `A < B`. -/
def subsorts : List (String × String) :=
  c.userSubsorts ++ fixedSubsorts ++ c.sortsBelowKItem.map (·, "KItem")

def le (a b : String) : Bool := a == b || c.subsorts.contains (a, b)

/-- All constructors: the fixed text's, then the user's. -/
def ctorSigs : List CtorSig := fixedCtors ++ c.ctors

end Semantics

def lookupSig (heads : List CtorSig) (f : String) : Option CtorSig := heads.find? (·.name == f)

end KCore

Value.text:
/-
  Ground values of a definition, generic in its semantics (M1.4; frozen layer).

  A configuration, and every value a function returns, is a ground constructor term: constructors
  of the definition (the fixed text's and the user's) applied to ground terms, injections
  `inj{A,B}` along declared subsorts, and domain values `\dv{S}("…")` of the base sorts. That is
  the set `GroundConfig` of Statements.lean describes (STATEMENTS.md §4), here as Lean data
  instead of KORE text.

  Representation (chosen deliberately; see findings/M1.4-generic-library.md, "Representation"):
  one untyped inductive `GroundTerm`, and the sort of a term computed by `Semantics.sortOf`, a
  structurally recursive function over the definition's data. `Value c s` is the subtype of the
  ground terms whose sort in `c` is `s`; `Config c` is `Value c topCellSort`. So the sort index is
  a predicate, not part of the inductive type:
  - every operation that the step reads (matching, substitution, evaluation) is untyped, as the
    clauses and rules of `Semantics` are (`Term` names sorts by strings);
  - equality and kernel evaluation are those of a plain first-order tree;
  - injections are data (`inj a b t`), not one constructor per subsort pair;
  - injection-normality (no `inj` directly under `inj`) is part of `sortOf`, as it is part of
    `groundSort`, so `Value c s` holds exactly one representation per element.
  Every function here is structurally recursive. Outside the frozen layer, in Execution.lean:
  the size of a ground term (the executable evaluation's fuel), `DecidableEq` for ground terms and
  values (used by `decide` in proofs and by the executable step), and `Value.ofTerm`; no
  statement reads them.
-/
import KcoreSpec.Core

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace KCore

/-- A ground constructor term: a constructor of the definition applied to ground terms
(`ctor f args`, `f` its KORE symbol), an injection `inj{a,b}(t)` (sort names without the `Sort`
prefix, as in `Term`), or a domain value `\dv{Sort s}(lit)` of a base sort. Whether it is
well-sorted is `Semantics.sortOf`. -/
inductive GroundTerm where
  | ctor (f : String) (args : List GroundTerm)
  | inj (a b : String) (t : GroundTerm)
  | dv (s : String) (lit : String)
  deriving Repr, Inhabited

namespace GroundTerm

def isInj : GroundTerm → Bool
  | .inj _ _ _ => true
  | _ => false

end GroundTerm

namespace Semantics
variable (c : Semantics)

/-- The base sorts without sort parameters: their elements are domain values. (MInt, the one
parametric base sort, is below no constructor's argument and below no sort, so no ground
configuration contains one of its values.) -/
def isDomainValueSort (s : String) : Bool := baseSorts.any fun (n, k) => n == s && k == 0

mutual
  /-- The sort of a ground term in `c`, or `none` if it is not one: a constructor of `c` applied
  to terms of its argument sorts; an injection `inj{a,b}` along a subsort `a < b` of a term of
  sort `a` that is not itself an injection (injection-normal); a domain value of a base sort.
  The same conditions as `groundSort` on KORE patterns (Statements.lean). -/
  def sortOf : GroundTerm → Option String
    | .ctor f ts => match lookupSig c.ctorSigs f with
      | some k => if sortsOf ts == some k.args then some k.result else none
      | none => none
    | .inj a b t => if c.subsorts.contains (a, b) && !t.isInj && sortOf t == some a then some b
                    else none
    | .dv s _ => if isDomainValueSort s then some s else none
    termination_by structural t => t
  def sortsOf : List GroundTerm → Option (List String)
    | [] => some []
    | t :: ts => match sortOf t, sortsOf ts with
      | some s, some ss => some (s :: ss)
      | _, _ => none
    termination_by structural ts => ts
end

end Semantics

/-- A value of sort `s` in `c`: a ground term whose sort is `s`. -/
def Value (c : Semantics) (s : String) : Type := { t : GroundTerm // c.sortOf t = some s }

/-- A configuration of `c`: a value of the configuration sort `GeneratedTopCell`. -/
abbrev Config (c : Semantics) : Type := Value c topCellSort

end KCore

Evaluation.text:
/-
  Matching and function evaluation, generic in the semantics (M1.4, made relational in M1.4c;
  frozen layer).

  - `matchTerm c p v`: the substitution under which the pattern `p` (a `Term` of a clause's or a
    rule's left-hand side) is the ground term `v`, if any. Patterns are first-order and, in a
    well-formed definition, linear, so there is at most one. An injection pattern `inj{a,b}(p)`
    matches every value `inj{a',b}(w)` with `a' ≤ a`: at `a' = a`, `p` matches `w`; at `a' < a`, `p`
    matches `inj{a',a}(w)`, the same element (Cons-Coh: `inj{a,b}(inj{a',a}(w)) = inj{a',b}(w)`).
    Matching is a structurally recursive function: it is decidable, and the evaluation relation
    below reads "no clause matches" as `matchTerms … = none`.
  - `Eval c f vs v`: the function `f` of `c` has the value `v` at the arguments `vs`. It is the
    first-match reading of the function's clauses (K's `owise` and the KORE equations' premises):
    the first clause whose argument patterns match `vs`, with σ, decides, and `v` is the value of
    its right-hand side under σ; if that right-hand side has no value, `f` has none at `vs` (no
    later clause is tried: the equations' premises read the arguments, not the right-hand
    sides). Where no clause matches, the catch-all clause, if `f` has one, gives the value.
  - `EvalTerm c σ t v`: the right-hand side `t` has the value `v` under σ: an application of a
    constructor of `c` builds the constructor term, any other application is a function call
    (`Eval`), injections are put in normal form, a variable is its value in σ.

  There is no fuel and no termination argument: an evaluation that does not terminate is one
  with no derivation, so the function has no value there. The executable evaluation with fuel
  that the reference step runs is in Execution.lean (checked layer), proved equal to this
  relation for the definitions it accepts (ExecutionTheory.lean).
-/
import KcoreSpec.Value

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace KCore

/-- A substitution: variable indices with their values. -/
abbrev Subst := List (Nat × GroundTerm)

/-- `inj{a,b}` applied to a value, in injection normal form: `inj{a,b}(inj{a',a}(w))` is
`inj{a',b}(w)` (Cons-Coh). -/
def injNormal (a b : String) : GroundTerm → GroundTerm
  | .inj a' _ w => .inj a' b w
  | v => .inj a b v

/-! ## Matching -/

mutual
  /-- The substitution under which the pattern is the value (as-pattern binders included), if
  any. -/
  def matchTerm (c : Semantics) : Term → GroundTerm → Option Subst
    | .var i, v => some [(i, v)]
    | .as p i, v => (matchTerm c p v).map (· ++ [(i, v)])
    | .app f ps, .ctor g vs => if f = g then matchTerms c ps vs else none
    | .inj a b p, .inj a' b' w =>
      if b = b' then
        if a' = a then matchTerm c p w
        else if c.le a' a then matchTerm c p (.inj a' a w)
        else none
      else none
    | .app _ _, .inj _ _ _ => none
    | .app _ _, .dv _ _ => none
    | .inj _ _ _, .ctor _ _ => none
    | .inj _ _ _, .dv _ _ => none
    termination_by structural p => p
  def matchTerms (c : Semantics) : List Term → List GroundTerm → Option Subst
    | [], [] => some []
    | p :: ps, v :: vs => match matchTerm c p v, matchTerms c ps vs with
      | some σ, some τ => some (σ ++ τ)
      | _, _ => none
    | [], _ :: _ => none
    | _ :: _, [] => none
    termination_by structural ps => ps
end

/-- The substitution of a catch-all clause: its variable `i` is the argument at position `i`. -/
def argSubst : Nat → List GroundTerm → Subst
  | _, [] => []
  | i, v :: vs => (i, v) :: argSubst (i + 1) vs

/-- The function of `c` named `f` (its first declaration; a well-formed definition declares each
once). -/
def Semantics.lookupFn (c : Semantics) (f : String) : Option Fn := c.fns.find? (·.label == f)

/-! ## Evaluation -/

mutual
  /-- `Eval c f vs v`: the function named `f` of `c` has the value `v` at `vs`. -/
  inductive Eval (c : Semantics) : String → List GroundTerm → GroundTerm → Prop where
    /-- The first clause `cl` whose patterns match `vs`, with σ, gives the value of its
    right-hand side under σ: the clauses before it do not match. -/
    | clause {f : String} {fn : Fn} {vs : List GroundTerm} {pre post : List Clause} {cl : Clause}
        {σ : Subst} {v : GroundTerm}
        (hfn : c.lookupFn f = some fn)
        (hcls : fn.clauses = pre ++ cl :: post)
        (hpre : ∀ cl' ∈ pre, matchTerms c cl'.pats vs = none)
        (hmatch : matchTerms c cl.pats vs = some σ)
        (hrhs : EvalTerm c σ cl.rhs v) : Eval c f vs v
    /-- Where no clause matches, the catch-all clause gives the value of its right-hand side,
    its variable `i` being the argument at position `i`. -/
    | owise {f : String} {fn : Fn} {vs : List GroundTerm} {o : Owise} {v : GroundTerm}
        (hfn : c.lookupFn f = some fn)
        (hnone : ∀ cl ∈ fn.clauses, matchTerms c cl.pats vs = none)
        (ho : fn.owise = some o)
        (hrhs : EvalTerm c (argSubst 0 vs) o.rhs v) : Eval c f vs v
  /-- `EvalTerm c σ t v`: the right-hand side `t` has the value `v` under σ. -/
  inductive EvalTerm (c : Semantics) : Subst → Term → GroundTerm → Prop where
    | var {σ : Subst} {i : Nat} {v : GroundTerm} (h : σ.lookup i = some v) : EvalTerm c σ (.var i) v
    /-- An application of a constructor of `c` builds the constructor term. -/
    | ctor {σ : Subst} {f : String} {ts : List Term} {vs : List GroundTerm}
        (h : (lookupSig c.ctorSigs f).isSome = true) (hts : EvalTerms c σ ts vs) :
        EvalTerm c σ (.app f ts) (.ctor f vs)
    /-- Any other application is a call of the function `f`. -/
    | call {σ : Subst} {f : String} {ts : List Term} {vs : List GroundTerm} {v : GroundTerm}
        (h : (lookupSig c.ctorSigs f).isSome = false) (hts : EvalTerms c σ ts vs)
        (hf : Eval c f vs v) : EvalTerm c σ (.app f ts) v
    /-- An injection, in normal form. -/
    | inj {σ : Subst} {a b : String} {t : Term} {v : GroundTerm} (h : EvalTerm c σ t v) :
        EvalTerm c σ (.inj a b t) (injNormal a b v)
  /-- `EvalTerms c σ ts vs`: the terms `ts` have the values `vs` under σ. -/
  inductive EvalTerms (c : Semantics) : Subst → List Term → List GroundTerm → Prop where
    | nil {σ : Subst} : EvalTerms c σ [] []
    | cons {σ : Subst} {t : Term} {ts : List Term} {v : GroundTerm} {vs : List GroundTerm}
        (h : EvalTerm c σ t v) (hs : EvalTerms c σ ts vs) : EvalTerms c σ (t :: ts) (v :: vs)
end

end KCore

Step.text:
/-
  The step relation of a definition, generic in its semantics (M1.4, relational evaluation since
  M1.4c; frozen layer).

  `Step c x y`: some rule of `c` rewrites the configuration `x` to `y`: its left-hand side matches
  `x` with a substitution σ, and its right-hand side has the value `y` under σ (`EvalTerm`,
  Evaluation.lean; requires and ensures are `\top` in F0, and rules have no priorities). One
  constructor for every definition; the rule is data (`r ∈ c.rules`). A rule whose right-hand side
  has no value under σ applies but gives no step, as a right-hand side `⊥` gives no successor in
  matching logic.

  The executable form, `successors c x` (one candidate per rule, in order), is in Execution.lean
  (checked layer); `step_iff` (ExecutionTheory.lean) proves `Step c x y ↔ y ∈ successors c x` once
  for every definition that `Semantics.evalReady` accepts.

  `Semantics.rulesApart`, the decidable condition under which `Step c` is deterministic, is in
  StepTheory.lean with `Step.deterministic` (checked layer; no statement reads it).
-/
import KcoreSpec.Evaluation

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace KCore

/-- One rewrite step of `c` between configurations: a rule of `c` whose left-hand side matches
`x` with σ and whose right-hand side evaluates to `y` under σ. -/
inductive Step (c : Semantics) : Config c → Config c → Prop where
  | rule {x y : Config c} (r : Rule) (mem : r ∈ c.rules) (σ : Subst)
      (hmatch : matchTerm c r.lhs x.val = some σ)
      (heval : EvalTerm c σ r.rhs y.val) : Step c x y

end KCore

PeanoCore.text:
/-
  The semantic core of the milestone subject `milestone-1/peano.k` as Lean data (the `Semantics`
  part of `peano`, PeanoSpec.lean). Reviewed per definition: it is what peano's statements
  (PeanoProperties.lean) are about. Split from PeanoSpec.lean on 2026-11-07, names and bodies
  unchanged, so that it imports only the core vocabulary (Core.lean).

  The rules of peano.k:
      rule <k> run(s(N)) => run(pred(s(N))) </k>
      rule <k> run(z) => done(z) </k>
  with `pred(s(N)) = N` and `pred(_) = z [owise]`, as kompile compiled them (the as-patterns
  `#as Gen4` and the counter-cell variable are kompile's).
  That this data is peano.k is checked by the kernel through the emitted KORE: `peano.emit = kore`
  (test/F0Check.lean), where `peano = ⟨peanoCore, peanoPres, ⟨[none]⟩⟩`.
-/
import KcoreSpec.Core

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace KCore.Peano

def tz : Term := .app "Lblz" []
def ts (t : Term) : Term := .app "Lbls" [t]
def tpred (t : Term) : Term := .app "Lblpred" [t]
def trun (t : Term) : Term := .app "Lblrun" [t]
def tdone (t : Term) : Term := .app "Lbldone" [t]

/-- `<generatedTop> <k> inj{State,KItem}(st) ~> . </k> counter </generatedTop>`. -/
def tcfg (st counter : Term) : Term :=
  .app "Lbl'-LT-'generatedTop'-GT-'"
    [.app kCellLabel [.app "kseq" [.inj "State" "KItem" st, .app "dotk" []]], counter]

/-- `pred(s(N)) = N`, `pred(_) = z [owise]`. -/
def predFn : Fn :=
  { label := "Lblpred", args := ["Nat"], result := "Nat"
    clauses := [{ vars := ["Nat"], pats := [ts (.var 0)], rhs := .var 0 }]
    owise := some { vars := ["Nat"], rhs := tz } }

def peanoCore : Semantics :=
  { userSorts := ["Nat", "State", "Val"]
    ctors := [⟨"Lblz", [], "Nat"⟩, ⟨"Lbls", ["Nat"], "Nat"⟩, ⟨"Lblrun", ["Nat"], "State"⟩,
              ⟨"Lbldone", ["Val"], "State"⟩]
    fns := [predFn]
    userSubsorts := [("Nat", "Val")]
    pgmSort := "State"
    rules :=
      -- <k> run(s(N) #as Gen4) => run(pred(Gen4)) </k>
      [{ vars := ["Nat", "Nat", "GeneratedCounterCell"]
         lhs := tcfg (trun (.as (ts (.var 0)) 1)) (.var 2)
         rhs := tcfg (trun (tpred (.var 1))) (.var 2) },
       -- <k> run(z #as Gen4) => done(Gen4) </k>
       { vars := ["Nat", "GeneratedCounterCell"]
         lhs := tcfg (trun (.as tz 0)) (.var 1)
         rhs := tcfg (tdone (.inj "Nat" "Val" (.var 0))) (.var 1) }] }

end KCore.Peano

PeanoLibrary.text:
/-
  The readable surface of peano over the generic library (M1.4, relational since M1.4c; frozen layer, per
  definition).

  Everything here is an abbreviation of the generic definitions applied to `peanoCore`
  (PeanoCore.lean), of the kind a generator writes from the definition's data: names for its
  constructors as ground terms (`@[match_pattern]`, so they can be used in patterns), for its
  configuration shape, and for its step and its function. The names of its rules (`runSucc`,
  `runZero`, `rules_eq`), which only the per-rule tactic reads, and the tactic
  `peano_step_cases` are in PeanoTactic.lean (checked layer).
-/
import KcoreSpec.PeanoCore
import KcoreSpec.Step

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace KCore.Peano.Ground

open KCore

/-! ## Values -/

@[match_pattern, reducible] def z : GroundTerm := .ctor "Lblz" []
@[match_pattern, reducible] def s (n : GroundTerm) : GroundTerm := .ctor "Lbls" [n]
@[match_pattern, reducible] def run (n : GroundTerm) : GroundTerm := .ctor "Lblrun" [n]
@[match_pattern, reducible] def done (v : GroundTerm) : GroundTerm := .ctor "Lbldone" [v]
/-- A `Nat` as a `Val` (the subsort `Nat < Val`): `inj{Nat,Val}(n)`. -/
@[match_pattern, reducible] def natVal (n : GroundTerm) : GroundTerm := .inj "Nat" "Val" n
/-- The counter cell `<generatedCounter> i </generatedCounter>`. -/
@[match_pattern, reducible] def counter (i : GroundTerm) : GroundTerm :=
  .ctor "Lbl'-LT-'generatedCounter'-GT-'" [i]
/-- An `Int` domain value. -/
@[match_pattern, reducible] def int (lit : String) : GroundTerm := .dv "Int" lit
/-- `<generatedTop> k ctr </generatedTop>`: the top cell, of the k cell `k` and the counter cell
`ctr`. -/
@[match_pattern, reducible] def top (k ctr : GroundTerm) : GroundTerm :=
  .ctor "Lbl'-LT-'generatedTop'-GT-'" [k, ctr]
/-- `<generatedTop> <k> st ~> . </k> ctr </generatedTop>`: peano's configurations. -/
@[match_pattern, reducible] def cfg (st ctr : GroundTerm) : GroundTerm :=
  top (.ctor "Lbl'-LT-'k'-GT-'" [.ctor "kseq" [.inj "State" "KItem" st, .ctor "dotk" []]]) ctr

/-! ## The semantics -/

abbrev Config : Type := KCore.Config peanoCore
abbrev Step : Config → Config → Prop := KCore.Step peanoCore
/-- `Pred n v`: `pred(n)` has the value `v` (the generic evaluation relation). -/
abbrev Pred (n v : GroundTerm) : Prop := Eval peanoCore "Lblpred" [n] v

end KCore.Peano.Ground

PeanoProperties.text:
/-
  Properties of peano, stated over the generic definitions (M1.4, relational since M1.4c; frozen
  layer).

  Each property is a `def X.statement : Prop`; its proof is the theorem `X` in PeanoProofs.lean
  (checked layer). Kept apart so that the elaboration of the frozen statements can be measured
  without the proofs (findings/M1.4-generic-library.md, findings/M1.4c-relational-eval.md).
  - `deterministic`: a configuration has at most one successor;
  - `pred_succ`, `pred_owise`: the two equations of `pred` over the evaluation relation:
    `pred(s(N))` has the value `N`, and, for every N not of the form `s(_)`, `pred(N)` has the
    value `z` (its `owise` clause), over every ground term N (uniqueness of the value is the
    generic `Eval.det`);
  - `doneHoldsZero_preserved`: every step keeps "if the k cell holds `done(v)`, then v is `z`";
  - `counter_preserved`: every step keeps the counter cell: if it holds `ctr` before, it holds
    `ctr` after.
  Non-vacuity witnesses, stated over `Step` directly (not through `refStep`):
  - `step_run_succ`, `step_run_zero`: `run(s(z))` steps to `run(z)`, and `run(z)` to `done(z)`;
    so `Step` is not empty, and the antecedent of `doneHoldsZero` is reached by a step;
  - `stuck_done`: `done(z)` is a configuration with no successor; so `Step` does not relate
    every configuration to something;
  - `doneHoldsZero_fails`: some configuration (`done(s(z))`) does not satisfy `doneHoldsZero`;
    so the invariant is not a property of every configuration.
-/
import KcoreSpec.PeanoLibrary

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace KCore.Peano.Ground

open KCore

/-- Determinism: a configuration has at most one successor. -/
def deterministic.statement : Prop := ∀ x y y' : Config, Step x y → Step x y' → y = y'

/-- `pred(s(N)) = N`. -/
def pred_succ.statement : Prop := ∀ N : GroundTerm, Pred (s N) N

/-- `pred(N) = z` where N is not `s(_)` (the `owise` clause). -/
def pred_owise.statement : Prop := ∀ N : GroundTerm, (∀ M, N ≠ s M) → Pred N z

/-- If the k cell holds `done(v)`, then v is `z` (as a `Val`). -/
def doneHoldsZero (x : Config) : Prop := ∀ v ctr, x.val = cfg (done v) ctr → v = natVal z

/-- Every step keeps `doneHoldsZero`. -/
def doneHoldsZero_preserved.statement : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : Config, Step x y → doneHoldsZero x → doneHoldsZero y

/-- The counter cell of `x` holds `ctr`. -/
def counterIs (ctr : GroundTerm) (x : Config) : Prop := ∃ k, x.val = top k ctr

/-- Every step keeps the counter cell. -/
def counter_preserved.statement : Prop :=
  ∀ (ctr : GroundTerm) (x y : Config), Step x y → counterIs ctr x → counterIs ctr y

/-! ## Non-vacuity witnesses

Each says that a particular configuration exists (its ground term has the configuration sort)
and how it steps. The counter cell is the one krust's initial configuration has. -/

/-- `<generatedCounter> 0 </generatedCounter>`. -/
def ctr0 : GroundTerm := counter (int "0")

/-- Witness: `run(s(z))` steps to `run(z)` (rule 1, with `pred(s(z))` evaluating to `z`). -/
def step_run_succ.statement : Prop :=
  ∃ x y : Config, x.val = cfg (run (s z)) ctr0 ∧ y.val = cfg (run z) ctr0 ∧ Step x y

/-- Witness: `run(z)` steps to `done(z)` (rule 2), a configuration whose k cell holds `done(_)`. -/
def step_run_zero.statement : Prop :=
  ∃ x y : Config, x.val = cfg (run z) ctr0 ∧ y.val = cfg (done (natVal z)) ctr0 ∧ Step x y

/-- Witness: `done(z)` is a configuration, and it has no successor. -/
def stuck_done.statement : Prop :=
  ∃ x : Config, x.val = cfg (done (natVal z)) ctr0 ∧ ∀ y : Config, ¬ Step x y

/-- Witness: `done(s(z))` is a configuration that does not satisfy `doneHoldsZero`. -/
def doneHoldsZero_fails.statement : Prop :=
  ∃ x : Config, x.val = cfg (done (natVal (s z))) ctr0 ∧ ¬ doneHoldsZero x

end KCore.Peano.Ground

PeanoProofs.text:
/-
  Proofs of the peano properties (M1.4, relational since M1.4c; checked layer): the baseline that
  an optimization loop starts from. Each is an instance of a generic theorem (StepTheory.lean),
  a constructor of the evaluation relation, or a use of the per-rule tactic; nothing about peano
  is proved here that is not one of the statements.
-/
import KcoreSpec.PeanoProperties
import KcoreSpec.PeanoTactic
import KcoreSpec.ExecutionTheory

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace KCore.Peano.Ground

open KCore

/-- From the generic theorem: peano's two rules do not overlap (decided on its data). -/
theorem deterministic : ∀ x y y' : Config, Step x y → Step x y' → y = y' :=
  fun _ _ _ => Step.deterministic (c := peanoCore) (by decide +kernel)

/-- The first clause of `pred` matches `s(N)`, binding its variable to `N`. -/
theorem pred_succ : ∀ N : GroundTerm, Pred (s N) N := fun _ =>
  .clause (fn := predFn) (pre := []) (post := []) rfl rfl (fun _ h => (nomatch h)) rfl (.var rfl)

/-- No clause of `pred` matches N, so its catch-all clause gives `z`. -/
theorem pred_owise : ∀ N : GroundTerm, (∀ M, N ≠ s M) → Pred N z := fun N hN => by
  have hm : matchTerms peanoCore [ts (.var 0)] [N] = none := by
    cases h : matchTerms peanoCore [ts (.var 0)] [N] with
    | none => rfl
    | some σ =>
      exfalso
      simp only [ts, matchTerms_cons, matchTerm_app, matchTerms_nil, matchTerm_var, List.cons.injEq] at h
      destruct_hyps
      subst_vars
      exact hN _ rfl
  exact .owise (fn := predFn) rfl (fun _ h => by rw [List.mem_singleton.mp h]; exact hm) rfl
    (.ctor rfl .nil)

/-- By the per-rule tactic: rule `runSucc` leaves `run(_)` in the k cell, rule `runZero` puts
`done(z)` there. -/
theorem doneHoldsZero_preserved :
    ∀ x y : Config, Step x y → doneHoldsZero x → doneHoldsZero y := by
  intro x y h _ v ctr hy
  peano_step_cases h []
  all_goals rfl

/-- By the per-rule tactic: both rules copy the counter cell. -/
theorem counter_preserved :
    ∀ (ctr : GroundTerm) (x y : Config), Step x y → counterIs ctr x → counterIs ctr y := by
  intro ctr x y h ⟨k, hk⟩
  peano_step_cases h []
  all_goals exact ⟨_, rfl⟩

/-! ## The non-vacuity witnesses

Through `step_iff`: peano's data satisfies `evalReady` (decided by the kernel), so `Step x y` is
`y ∈ successors peanoCore x`, and the kernel computes `successors` on the closed configurations. -/

theorem step_run_succ : step_run_succ.statement := by
  let x : Config := ⟨cfg (run (s z)) ctr0, by decide +kernel⟩
  let y : Config := ⟨cfg (run z) ctr0, by decide +kernel⟩
  have hs : successors peanoCore x = [y] := by decide +kernel
  refine ⟨x, y, rfl, rfl, (step_iff (c := peanoCore) (by decide +kernel)).mpr ?_⟩
  rw [hs]
  exact List.mem_singleton_self _

theorem step_run_zero : step_run_zero.statement := by
  let x : Config := ⟨cfg (run z) ctr0, by decide +kernel⟩
  let y : Config := ⟨cfg (done (natVal z)) ctr0, by decide +kernel⟩
  have hs : successors peanoCore x = [y] := by decide +kernel
  refine ⟨x, y, rfl, rfl, (step_iff (c := peanoCore) (by decide +kernel)).mpr ?_⟩
  rw [hs]
  exact List.mem_singleton_self _

theorem stuck_done : stuck_done.statement := by
  let x : Config := ⟨cfg (done (natVal z)) ctr0, by decide +kernel⟩
  have hs : successors peanoCore x = [] := by decide +kernel
  refine ⟨x, rfl, fun y h => ?_⟩
  have hy := (step_iff (c := peanoCore) (by decide +kernel)).mp h
  rw [hs] at hy
  cases hy

theorem doneHoldsZero_fails : doneHoldsZero_fails.statement :=
  ⟨⟨cfg (done (natVal (s z))) ctr0, by decide +kernel⟩, rfl,
    fun h => absurd (h (natVal (s z)) ctr0 rfl) (by decide)⟩

end KCore.Peano.Ground

PeanoTactic.text:
/-
  `peano_step_cases`: one goal per rule of peano (M1.4; checked layer, per definition). It is the
  generic `step_cases` (StepTactic.lean) given peano's rules by name (`runSucc`, `runZero`, and
  `rules_eq`, which checks by `rfl` that they are peano's), the names of PeanoLibrary.lean, and
  peano's subsort list decided once on its data (`subsorts_eq`), which the tactic's side
  conditions read.
-/
import KcoreSpec.PeanoLibrary
import KcoreSpec.StepTactic

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace KCore.Peano.Ground

open KCore

/-! ## Peano's rules by name (moved from PeanoLibrary.lean on 2026-11-07; no statement reads them) -/

/-- `rule <k> run(s(N) #as Gen4) => run(pred(Gen4)) </k>` -/
def runSucc : Rule :=
  { vars := ["Nat", "Nat", "GeneratedCounterCell"]
    lhs := tcfg (trun (.as (ts (.var 0)) 1)) (.var 2)
    rhs := tcfg (trun (tpred (.var 1))) (.var 2) }

/-- `rule <k> run(z #as Gen4) => done(Gen4) </k>` -/
def runZero : Rule :=
  { vars := ["Nat", "GeneratedCounterCell"]
    lhs := tcfg (trun (.as tz 0)) (.var 1)
    rhs := tcfg (tdone (.inj "Nat" "Val" (.var 0))) (.var 1) }

theorem rules_eq : peanoCore.rules = [runSucc, runZero] := rfl

/-! ## The tactic -/

/-- The subsort pairs of peano (decided on its data). -/
theorem subsorts_eq : peanoCore.subsorts =
    [("Nat", "Val"), ("KCell", "KCellOpt"), ("GeneratedCounterCell", "GeneratedCounterCellOpt"),
     ("Bool", "KItem"), ("GeneratedCounterCell", "KItem"), ("GeneratedCounterCellOpt", "KItem"),
     ("GeneratedTopCell", "KItem"), ("GeneratedTopCellFragment", "KItem"), ("Int", "KItem"),
     ("KCell", "KItem"), ("KCellOpt", "KItem"), ("KConfigVar", "KItem"), ("List", "KItem"),
     ("Map", "KItem"), ("Nat", "KItem"), ("Set", "KItem"), ("State", "KItem"), ("Val", "KItem")] := by
  decide +kernel

end KCore.Peano.Ground

/-- `peano_step_cases h [extra…]`: one goal per rule of peano for `h : Step x y`. -/
macro "peano_step_cases " h:ident " [" ls:Lean.Parser.Tactic.simpLemma,* "]" : tactic =>
  `(tactic| step_cases $h [KCore.Peano.Ground.rules_eq, KCore.Peano.Ground.subsorts_eq,
      KCore.Peano.Ground.runSucc,
      KCore.Peano.Ground.runZero, KCore.Peano.tcfg, KCore.Peano.trun, KCore.Peano.ts,
      KCore.Peano.tz, KCore.Peano.tpred, KCore.Peano.tdone, KCore.kCellLabel, $ls,*])

evalWithFuel.text:
/-- `f` at `vs` with `fuel` for its self calls (one unit per nested self call). -/
def evalWithFuel (c : Semantics) (other : String → List GroundTerm → Option GroundTerm) (f : Fn) :
    Nat → List GroundTerm → Option GroundTerm
  | 0, _ => none
  | n + 1, vs => applyClauses c other (evalWithFuel c other f n) f vs

fnFuel.text:
/-- The fuel of a call of `f` at `vs`: one more than the size of the argument at its decreasing
position (one when there is none). -/
def Fn.fuel (f : Fn) (vs : List GroundTerm) : Nat :=
  (match f.decreasingArg with
   | some i => (vs[i]?.map GroundTerm.size).getD 0
   | none => 0) + 1

successors.text:
/-- The result of applying the rule `r` to the ground term `x`, if its left-hand side matches. -/
def Rule.apply (c : Semantics) (r : Rule) (x : GroundTerm) : Option GroundTerm :=
  match matchTerm c r.lhs x with
  | some σ => evalTerm c (eval c) σ r.rhs
  | none => none

/-- The successors of a configuration, one candidate per rule of `c`, in order. -/
def successors (c : Semantics) (x : Config c) : List (Config c) :=
  c.rules.filterMap fun r => (r.apply c x.val).bind (Value.ofTerm c topCellSort)

evalReady.text:
/-- The condition under which `eval` is `Eval` (ExecutionTheory.lean): the functions' labels are
distinct; every function's fuel suffices (`Fn.ready`); and no function calls one declared after
it (unless that label is a constructor's, which is never a call). -/
def Semantics.evalReady (c : Semantics) : Bool :=
  let rec go : List Fn → Bool
    | [] => true
    | f :: fs => f.ready &&
        fs.all (fun g => (lookupSig c.ctorSigs g.label).isSome || f.callsNone g.label) && go fs
  nodup (c.fns.map (·.label)) && go c.fns

stepIff.text:
theorem eval_iff (hr : c.evalReady = true) {f : String} {vs : List GroundTerm} {v : GroundTerm} :
    eval c f vs = some v ↔ Eval c f vs v :=
  ⟨eval_sound (evalReady_nodup hr), Eval.complete hr⟩

theorem evalTerm_eval_iff (hr : c.evalReady = true) {σ : Subst} {t : Term} {v : GroundTerm} :
    evalTerm c (eval c) σ t = some v ↔ EvalTerm c σ t v :=
  ⟨evalTerm_sound (fun _ _ _ _ h => eval_sound (evalReady_nodup hr) h) t,
   EvalTerm.complete hr (fun _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ h => h)⟩

/-- The executable step is the frozen one, for every definition `evalReady` accepts. -/
theorem step_iff (hr : c.evalReady = true) {x y : Config c} : Step c x y ↔ y ∈ successors c x := by

stepIffWf.text:
/-- For a well-formed definition, the executable step (and so `refStep`) is the frozen `Step`. -/
theorem step_iff_wf {d : Definition} (hwf : wf d = true) {x y : Config d.sem} :
    Step d.sem x y ↔ y ∈ successors d.sem x :=
  step_iff (wf_evalReady' hwf)

rulesApart.text:
/-- No sort has two incomparable supersorts: if `x ≤ a` and `x ≤ b`, then `a ≤ b` or `b ≤ a`
(checked over the declared subsort pairs, the only way `x ≤ a` holds for `x ≠ a`). -/
def noDiamonds : Bool :=
  c.subsorts.all fun (x, a) => c.subsorts.all fun (x', b) =>
    !(x == x') || c.le a b || c.le b a

/-- No two rules' left-hand sides overlap, and the subsort order has no diamonds. -/
def rulesApart : Bool :=
  c.noDiamonds && (pairs c.rules).all fun (r, r') => !overlap c.le r.lhs r'.lhs

stepDeterministic.text:
theorem Step.deterministic (h : c.rulesApart = true) {x y y' : Config c}
    (h₁ : Step c x y) (h₂ : Step c x y') : y = y' := by

evalDet.text:
theorem Eval.det {f : String} {vs : List GroundTerm} {v v' : GroundTerm}
      (h : Eval c f vs v) (h' : Eval c f vs v') : v = v' :=

stepCasesDoc.text:
`step_cases`: one goal per rule of a definition (M1.4, relational since M1.4c; checked layer,
  generic).

      step_cases h [defs…]

  For `h : Step c x y` with `c` a definition whose rules `defs` unfold to a literal list (a
  definition's surface gives the lemma `rules_eq : c.rules = [r₁, …, rₙ]` and the rules' names),
  with `x` and `y` local variables, it leaves one goal per rule rᵢ, in which
  - `x` is the rule's left-hand side instantiated by the match (`x` is replaced by it
    everywhere), with one local variable per pattern variable, and
  - `y` is the rule's right-hand side, its evaluation relation (`EvalTerm`) inverted
    constructor by constructor; a function call stays a hypothesis `Eval c f vs v`, unless one
    of `defs` rewrites it (for example `Eval c f [s N] v ↔ v = N`, from an equation and
    `Eval.iff_of`). Equations between ground terms that result (from the inversion, or from a
    hypothesis that fixed `x` or `y`) are compared constructor by constructor: a clash closes
    the goal, agreement substitutes.
  The rules are data: the split is the membership `r ∈ c.rules` unfolded by `defs`, the match and
  the evaluation are inverted by the generic lemmas of StepTheory.lean, so nothing is proved per
  definition. An injection pattern from a sort with nothing below it is inverted with the side
  condition `c.below a = []`, and a head is told apart as a constructor or a function by
  `lookupSig c.ctorSigs f`, both decided by the kernel (cheaper when `defs` has the
  definition's subsort list, `c.subsorts = [...]`).

theoremA.text: theorem theoremA (d : Definition) : TheoremA d (refStep d.sem) := sorry

refSem.text:
/-- `peanoCore` with the user sorts and the user constructors in the reference KORE's
declaration order; every other field is `peanoCore`'s. -/
def refSem : Semantics :=
  { peanoCore with
    userSorts := ["Val", "Nat", "State"]
    ctors := [⟨"Lbldone", ["Val"], "State"⟩, ⟨"Lblrun", ["Nat"], "State"⟩,
              ⟨"Lbls", ["Nat"], "Nat"⟩, ⟨"Lblz", [], "Nat"⟩] }

parseRefSem.text:
theorem parse_ref_sem : (Parse.parse refKore).map (·.sem) = some refSem := by decide +kernel

theorem wf_parse_ref : (Parse.parse refKore).map wf = some true := by decide +kernel

stepOnRefSem.text:
/-- The step relation of a core, read on ground terms: `x` and `y` are configurations and
`Step c x y`. -/
def StepOn (c : Semantics) (x y : GroundTerm) : Prop :=
